newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina firm against U.S patent pressure-report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina firm against U.S patent pressure-report.

text.p: Argentina will not cede to U.S. pressure to change its patent laws, Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella said in a newspaper interview published Wednesday.

"The United States has been getting very heavy on the subject of patents," Di Tella told afternoon paper La Razon, "They have not only insisted that we comply with requirements established by GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade), but on top of that they want things that go beyond GATT."
He said the subject of patents will probably crop up in U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Argentina planned for later this year, but added: "We are not going to budge."
The United States announced in January that it was withdrawing half of Argentina's duty-free benefits as Argentine laws failed to protect U.S. drug firms.
Argentine media estimated the move would cost $10-20 million in lost exports.
The United States said that new intellectual property laws passed in 1995 and 1996 still allowed Argentine firms to copy foreign companies' drugs.
